clue.text: Cheaper retail outlets ignore husbands

parts.note: to discount something is to disregard it or leave it out of account
to husband resources is to conserve them, to keep them in reserve, so husbands means stores

explanation.surface: Bargain shops are said to turn away married men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husbands' looks like a plural noun for married men but is the verb meaning to save or keep in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: These are shops selling goods below the usual price, so they are the cheaper places to buy.

clue.text: Severe doctor takes wine cold

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A stern physician drinks his wine chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are harsh and extreme ones, close in sense to severe.

clue.text: Cheering up?

parts.note: read not as making someone happier but as an audience applauding while on its feet, risen up out of its seats

explanation.definitionFit: An ovation given by an audience that rises from its seats is applause delivered while upright.

clue.text: Confesses to having topless robes

indicators.note: topless says the first letter, the top of the down entry, is taken off the word for robes

parts.note: gowns are long robes, as worn by academics or judges

explanation.surface: Someone admits to wearing robes with nothing on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to having' merely links; 'own to' or 'own up' is an idiom for admitting something.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, in the sense of acknowledging or admitting, is an old synonym for confess.

clue.text: Trap let off that can sting

parts.note: a net is a device for trapping fish or animals

indicators.note: off here means wrong or awry, telling us the letters of let are jumbled

explanation.surface: A snare, once released, might give you a sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns LET into TLE, placed after NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging nettle is a common weed whose hairs inject an irritant when touched.

clue.text: Broadcaster, chap supporting top players in tournament

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, so the word for chap comes after the other piece

parts.note: seeds are the highest-ranked players in a tennis or similar tournament, kept apart in the draw
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A radio presenter is a fellow backing the leading players at a tennis event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests radio or TV, but here it means one who scatters seed over a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedsman sows or sells seed, and to broadcast originally meant to scatter seed widely by hand.

clue.text: Exaggeration in Whitehall, say, is finished pro tem

parts.note: something that is over has come to an end
pro tem, short for pro tempore, means for the time being, as with an acting chairman standing in temporarily

explanation.surface: Civil service spin in Whitehall is a stopgap measure that has now ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall seems to be the seat of British government, but it is also the London theatre known for Brian Rix's broad farces, where hamming it up was the house style.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamming it up on stage, playing a part with too much emphasis, is a theatrical form of exaggeration.

clue.text: Exit ma, with tin-opener trouble, for carrying out tests

indicators.note: trouble with the tin-opener suggests things going wrong, a sign that the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Mum is told to leave because her struggles with the can opener are holding up the lab work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; 'trouble' rearranges EXITMA and TINOPENER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Experimentation is the process of conducting trials to see what happens, that is, running tests.

clue.text: Reportedly caters to these zoo favourites

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for caters to is heard spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: to pander to someone is to cater to their whims or wishes

explanation.surface: A zookeeper supposedly indulges the animals visitors love most.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for caters to and the bears' name sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant black-and-white bears from China have long been star attractions at zoos.

clue.text: Opposed to the Turkish ruler this month

parts.note: an aga was a military commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire
inst., short for instant, means of the current month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A sultan's subject objects to something happening this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is an old commercial abbreviation: 'your letter of the 5th inst.' means the 5th of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against a proposal is to oppose it, so the word replaces opposed to in any sentence.

clue.text: River palm waving and other short stories?

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, flowing through Exeter

indicators.note: a palm waving in the breeze moves about, so its letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A Devon river and a swaying palm tree feature in some brief tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' makes MPLA from PALM; 'and other' is a link, hinting there are more stories of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempla are illustrative anecdotes, the moral tales a medieval preacher used to make a point in a sermon.

clue.text: Businesslike orderly

explanation.surface: An efficient manager runs a well-arranged office.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean neat, efficient and well arranged, as in a neat sum or a well-kept desk.

clue.text: Tall riders injured? How unfortunate!

indicators.note: riders who are injured are hurt or damaged, a sign that the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Jockeys who are too tall end up getting hurt, which is a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is only a link, turning the definition into an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred means born under an unlucky star, so doomed to misfortune.

clue.text: See twister turning out with it in the city

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters being turned over and rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Watch a tornado swirl away from an urban street.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone streetwise is shrewd and savvy about the ways of urban life, hip to the city.

clue.text: Great Dane that flopped on the beach

definitions.text: Great Dane that flopped on the beach

parts.words: Great Dane that flopped on the beach
parts.note: not a large dog sprawled on the sand but a Danish king of England who, according to legend, ordered the incoming tide to halt and failed

explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh-century king of Denmark and England is famed for the tale of commanding the waves to retreat.

clue.text: Period in canyon for diversions

indicators.note: in places the word for period within the word for canyon

parts.note: a pass is a narrow route through mountains, like a gorge or canyon
a period is a time or era

explanation.surface: A spell spent in a gorge makes for some recreations.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastimes are hobbies or amusements that pass the time pleasantly, much like diversions.

clue.text: Rising again and making a note to get to know where one is

definitions.text: get to know where one is

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
orient as an adjective means rising, like the sun in the east

explanation.surface: Climbing up once more and jotting something down to find one's bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' hints that RE- is also the prefix for again; 'making' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorient oneself is to find one's bearings again, working out one's position.

clue.text: Mean little Edward to shut up

parts.note: close means stingy or mean with money
Ted is a short pet name for Edward

explanation.surface: A stingy young Ted is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' suggests 'be quiet', but here it means confined to a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: To be closeted is to be shut away in private, as in closeted with a lawyer.

clue.text: No home bird, this slightly mad type

explanation.surface: A wandering bird that never builds a nest is a bit dotty.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird lays its eggs in other birds' nests rather than making a home of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the European brood parasite, and a crazy or eccentric person is also called by its name.

clue.text: Loosen a French tie?

parts.note: un is the French masculine word for a
a knot is a tie in a rope or string

explanation.surface: A Parisian slackens his neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo the knots in something frees it up, making it less tight.

clue.text: Handles of brushes

explanation.surface: The grips of paintbrushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Handles means feels with the fingers; brushes means light contacts, each a kind of gentle contact.

clue.text: Japanese art that may produce a little ash?

definitions.text: Japanese art that may produce a little ash?

parts.words: Japanese art that may produce a little ash?
parts.note: ash suggests cinders from a fire, but here it is a tree, kept miniature by the Japanese craft of pruning potted trees

explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese practice of growing dwarfed trees in pots could yield a miniature version of a tall woodland species.

clue.text: Gossip to go on strike

parts.note: to go on is to talk at length, to chatter
to box is to strike with the fists, or box someone's ears

explanation.surface: A rumour-monger urges workers to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but means hit; 'Gossip' is a person here.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks incessantly and spreads tittle-tattle is a gossip.

clue.text: Some solvent abuse is beyond the pale

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Glue-sniffing is unacceptable behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom, unacceptable in polite society, is outside the bounds of decency.

clue.text: There's comfort in herbal medicine

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the words herbal medicine, spanning both

explanation.surface: Herbal remedies bring some relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm is a soothing ointment and, figuratively, anything that brings solace.

clue.text: Alternative to providing diamonds in an opening

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
if means on condition that, providing
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Another option is to fit gems in a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or mouth, as of a tube or the body.

clue.text: Son, prodigal, is fawning

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
prodigal means wastefully extravagant, as lavish spending is

explanation.surface: The prodigal son is now grovelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the biblical prodigal son returning home humbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish behaviour is servile and obsequious, the manner of someone fawning.

clue.text: Internet at men's organization for amusements

indicators.note: organization means arranging into order, a sign that these letters are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: Online sites at a men's club are for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in men's is ignored; its S joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainments are shows or diversions that amuse people.
